title: Minimal-interval reflection of inert factorization categories
statement:
Use the small quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], the full coherent factorization category $\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)$ of [def-coef-operadic-weak-approximation], and coherent adjunction data (unit, counit and the two triangle $2$-simplices) as in [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data]. Let $g:M\to O$ be an inert-preserving categorical fibration of small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads, with $O$ ordinary, and let $C\in M$. For any arrow $\alpha:X\to g(C)$ lying over $[n]\to[k]$, let $\phi:[k]\to[n]$ be its opposite base map and put $a=\phi(0)$, $b=\phi(k)$, $r=b-a$. Let $\mathcal A_0\subseteq\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)$ be the full subcategory on factorizations $(\beta:D\to C,\gamma:X\to g(D))$ whose inert first edge $\gamma$ lies over the opposite of the inclusion $[r]\hookrightarrow[n]$, $j\mapsto a+j$. Then its full inclusion $i:\mathcal A_0\to\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)$ has a left adjoint $R$, given by coherent adjunction data $R\dashv i$ in the sense of [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data], with unit $\eta:\operatorname{id}\to iR$ and equivalence counit $Ri\simeq\operatorname{id}$. More precisely, for an object $A=(\beta,\gamma)$ with base interval $[t,t+m]$ of $\gamma$, there is an inert restriction $q:D\to D_0$ over the opposite of $[r]\hookrightarrow[m]$, $j\mapsto a-t+j$, and a compatible factorization $\beta\simeq\beta_0q$. The object $R(A)$ can be taken equivalent to $(\beta_0,g(q)\gamma)$, and the unit is represented by $q$ with its coherent triangles. For every $B\in\mathcal A_0$, precomposition with this unit induces a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A_0}(R(A),B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)}(A,iB).$$
The comparison edges in $\mathcal F_g(C,\alpha)$ are unrestricted; they are not required to be inert. No weak contractibility hypothesis on any lifting or factorization category is imposed. The case $r=0$ is included.

proof.text: Let $p_M:M\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and $p_O:O\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be the operad projections. For $A=(\beta:D\to C,\gamma:X\to g(D))$, write $p_O(\gamma)=J^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $J:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$, $J(u)=t+u$, and $p_M(\beta)=\psi^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its triangle gives $\phi=J\psi$, hence $t\leq a\leq b\leq t+m$. Define $\ell:[r]\hookrightarrow[m]$ by $\ell(v)=a-t+v$ and $\psi_0:[k]\to[r]$ by $\psi_0(v)=\phi(v)-a$. Then $\psi=\ell\psi_0$ and $J\ell(v)=a+v$. These formulas hold for noninjective $\phi$ and for $r=0$.

proof.text: The generalized-operad inert-lift axiom supplies a $p_M$-cocartesian edge $q:D\to D_0$ over $\ell^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply the cocartesian mapping-square criterion with target $C$. On the base-arrow component $\psi_0^{\mathrm{op}}$ it says that precomposition gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_M^{\psi_0^{\mathrm{op}}}(D_0,C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_M^{\psi^{\mathrm{op}}}(D,C)$. Indeed the base is the nerve of an ordinary category, so its mapping spaces are discrete, and the prescribed component maps to the component of $\psi^{\mathrm{op}}$. Taking the homotopy fiber at $\beta$ gives a contractible space of pairs $(\beta_0,\beta_0q\simeq\beta)$. Choose such a pair; the triangle in the slice is part of this choice, rather than an equality only in the homotopy category.

proof.text: Because $g$ preserves inert edges, $g(q)$ is $p_O$-cocartesian. The composition/cancellation lemma implies that the composite $\gamma_0=g(q)\gamma$ is $p_O$-cocartesian. Its base is $(J\ell)^{\mathrm{op}}$, so its interval is exactly $[a,b]$. Applying $g$ to the chosen slice triangle and composing with the triangle of $A$ gives a coherent triangle $g(\beta_0)\gamma_0\simeq\alpha$. Thus $A_0=(\beta_0,\gamma_0)$ is an object of the full subcategory $\mathcal A_0$. The same pasting, retaining the compatibility simplex, gives an edge $\eta_A:A\to iA_0$ in the specified join-slice model, with comparison edge $q$. All compositions here are coherent compositions, not choices of strict equalities.

proof.text:
Here is the mapping-space calculation used below. Put $S=M_{/C}$, $T=O_{/g(C)}$, and $H=S\times_T T_{\alpha/}$ as in the definition of $\mathcal F$. The slice-right-fibration theorem makes $S,T$ quasicategories. The coslice-left-fibration theorem makes $T_{\alpha/}\to T$ a left fibration; its pullback $H\to S$ is again left, by projecting and filling each left-horn lifting problem. Opposite duality and the right-fibration morphism-space formula therefore give, naturally in two objects $A,B$ of $\mathcal F$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F}(A,B)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\gamma_B}\left(\operatorname{Map}_S(\beta,\beta_B)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_T(\alpha,g\beta_B)\right).$$
The map takes $h$ with its slice triangle to $(g h)\gamma$ with its pasted triangle. The fiber of $T_{\alpha/}$ at $g\beta_B$ is the left-pinched mapping model, naturally equivalent to the right-pinched one by opposite duality. Fullness gives the same mapping spaces in $H$ and $\mathcal F$. Likewise the cone mapping-fiber formula for a one-object diagram, transported through the join-slice/arrow-slice equivalence, gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_S(\beta,\beta_B)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\beta}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_M(D,D_B)\xrightarrow{\beta_B\circ-}\operatorname{Map}_M(D,C)\bigr).$$
These are natural equivalences of spaces with their homotopies, so subsequent fibers retain the compatibility of the triangles.

proof.text:
Fix $B\in\mathcal A_0$, so $D_B$ is over $[r]$. In the first fiber of Step 4, every comparison $h:D\to D_B$ has an opposite base map $u:[r]\to[m]$ satisfying $Ju(v)=a+v$, by the compatibility with $\gamma_B$. Since $J$ is injective, $u=\ell$ is forced. For a comparison out of $A_0$, the same equation forces the opposite base map to be $\operatorname{id}_{[r]}$. Higher homotopies in the base cannot change these maps since its mapping spaces are discrete. Apply the cocartesian mapping-square criterion for $q$ with targets $D_B$ and $C$. It gives equivalences on the two prescribed components
$$\operatorname{Map}_M^{\operatorname{id}}(D_0,D_B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_M^{\ell^{\mathrm{op}}}(D,D_B),\qquad \operatorname{Map}_M^{\psi_0^{\mathrm{op}}}(D_0,C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_M^{\psi^{\mathrm{op}}}(D,C).$$
Postcomposition with $\beta_B$ commutes with these equivalences up to its coherent composition homotopy. Homotopy-pullback invariance, taking fibers at $\beta_0$ and $\beta$ and using the chosen triangle, gives an equivalence between the corresponding base-map components of $\operatorname{Map}_S(\beta_0,\beta_B)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_S(\beta,\beta_B)$. This is the actual precomposition map along the slice edge represented by $q$.

source.place: Agent expansion of the minimal-interval restriction supporting Definition A.6.1 and Proposition A.6.3 / Erratum Proposition E.0.2; these propositions state the approximation criterion, not the reflector itself.

proof.text:
Use Step 4 once for $(A_0,B)$ and once for $(A,B)$. The equivalence of slice-mapping components in Step 5 lies over the same target space $\operatorname{Map}_T(\alpha,g\beta_B)$: the equality $\gamma_0=g(q)\gamma$ and the compatible slice triangle identify the two composition maps, with their homotopy. The fiber at $\gamma_B$ only meets these components, by the forced-base calculation of Step 5. Homotopy-pullback invariance therefore gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A_0}(A_0,B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F}(A,iB),$$
induced by precomposition with $\eta_A$. All mapping-fiber formulas and composition maps used above are natural in $B$; thus this is a natural equivalence on the full category $\mathcal A_0$, including higher simplices. In particular, there is no imposed inertness condition on $h$: its base map is forced by the triangles, while its edge in $M$ is unrestricted.

proof.text: For every $A$, Step 6 represents $B\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F}(A,iB)$ by $A_0$, with universal edge $\eta_A$. Apply the dual pointwise adjoint criterion to the full inclusion $i$. It assembles the representatives into a coherent functor $R$, the chosen universal edges into its unit, and supplies a counit and both coherent triangle identities, as required by the coherent-adjunction definition. This avoids choosing unrelated edge-level factorizations and asserting that they form a functor. For $A=iB$ with $B\in\mathcal A_0$, one has $t=a,m=r,\ell=\operatorname{id}$, so the identity restriction and $\beta_0=\beta_B$ can be used in Steps 2-3. The identity universal edge represents the functor $B'\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A_0}(B,B')$ by fullness. The universal property identifies $RiB$ with $B$, and its counit is this equivalence: applying the two representing equivalences to the identity maps gives inverse comparisons and both inverse homotopies. Hence the counit is a coherent equivalence.

source.place: Agent expansion of the minimal-interval restriction supporting Definition A.6.1 and Proposition A.6.3 / Erratum Proposition E.0.2; these propositions state the approximation criterion, not the reflector itself.

proof.text: If $r=0$, the map $\ell:[0]\hookrightarrow[m]$ selects the vertex $a-t$. It is an inert interval inclusion, so Steps 2-6 apply without modification. It need not be an identity: for $n=1,k=0,\phi(0)=0$ and an object with $t=0,m=1$, the restriction has base $[1]\to[0]$. If $n=0$, then $m=r=0$ and $\ell$ is an identity; if $\alpha$ is active, then $[a,b]=[0,n]$ forces every object to be minimal already. If $\mathcal F$ is empty the objectwise criterion is vacuous and gives the unique adjunction between empty categories. No weak contractibility assumption about any factorization or lifting category was used.
